tagline: Graded with confidence, sold with proof
founded_place_size: Founded 2019 in Providence, Rhode Island; a four person consignment house
about: SlabVault Cards is a small consignment house that lists and settles graded collectibles for private sellers. Lots run from roughly 150 to 5,000 dollars per item, and buyers decide from the photograph alone, zooming into the holder, the label and the corners before they bid. Consignors shoot their own slabs on their own tables, so the house exists to bring many different rooms to one credible standard. Trust is the entire product: everything SlabVault presents has to read as accurate, unretouched and verifiable.
audience: Condition-literate collectors aged 25 to 60 who buy graded cards and comics at 150 to 5,000 dollars a lot, read the grade and certification line straight out of the image, and walk away from anything that looks staged or concealed.
price_positioning: Mid to upper consignment. Not a bulk reseller or a toy shop, and not a fine-art auction room. The presentation sits deliberately between the two: neutral, generous and evidential, never cheap and flashy, never gilded and theatrical.

palette.name: Slate Grey (primary ground)
palette.usage: The primary ground: the tile background or the stage around the slab. Also small secondary labels on Paper Neutral, as the consignor and condition labels on slabvault_lot_card.pdf. Never the lot number, title, grade line, certification line or condition note.

palette.name: Vault Charcoal (near-black text and frame)
palette.usage: All primary type (lot number, title, grade line, certification line and condition note), set on Paper Neutral as on slabvault_lot_card.pdf, plus thin frames and keylines, as around that ticket and its thumbnail. Never a ground or panel.

palette.name: Paper Neutral (light stage)
palette.usage: The ground under all type, as the ground of slabvault_lot_card.pdf, and optionally a light stage behind the slab. Never type.

palette.name: Signal Amber (single restrained accent)
palette.usage: The single restrained accent: at most one hairline rule or small marker per tile, as the one hairline under the masthead of slabvault_lot_card.pdf. Never type, a ground or a panel.

typography: SlabVault Cards holds one four step scale across the listing tiles and the printed tickets. Step 01 is the register print, the lot number in Redaction 35, the visibly dotted cut, at 44 px on 48 px leading, tracking -10 units, and it is the only degraded element on an otherwise crisp tile. Step 02 is the lot title in Söhne Buch at 30 px on 34 px, tracking -5 units, which is also the size Redaction Regular takes when a tile carries a heading. Step 03 is the grade line in Söhne Buch at 22 px on 32 px, tracking 0 with the measure capped at 65 characters, and it is never letterspaced. Step 04 is the certification line in Söhne Mono Regular at 18 px on 26 px, tracking +20 units. Printed tickets keep the same order at print sizes, lot number 18 pt and grade 9 pt.
voice: Plain, factual, collector to collector. States the grade, the grader and the condition without hype. Never breathless, never salesy. The photograph does the persuading.
brand_assets_status: SlabVault has never held a proper brand kit. What exists is a house note describing the palette in words (grey, black, one amber accent already used on the printed stationery and the sleeve ticket), the grading partner names spelled the way the graders require, and the sale details. There is no logo file, no type specimen and no template, so the house look has to be established fresh and held consistently across the listings, the printed tickets and the auction-week set.
values: Accuracy over polish. Show the item exactly as submitted, give every slab room to be read, and never add an edge, shine or shadow that was not there. The buyer's confidence is the asset the whole business protects.

type_system.tagline: Graded with confidence, sold with proof

scale.note: The register print. Redaction 35, the visibly dotted cut, is the only degraded element on an otherwise crisp tile, so the number reads as struck by the vault ledger before anything else. On the printed ticket the same line sets at 18 pt.
Redaction Regular, the clean cut, sets a tile heading at this same 30 px on 34 px where a tile carries one. The title always sits below the lot number, never above it.
Measure capped at 65 characters. The grade is never letterspaced, at any size, on screen or in print. On the printed ticket the grade sets at 9 pt.
Certification digits stay in Söhne Mono so a buyer can read them straight out of the image, digit by digit, without ambiguity.

type_system.signature_move: The register print. Every lot number runs in Redaction 35, the visibly dotted cut, at 44 px on 48 px, the single degraded element on an otherwise crisp tile, so it looks struck by the vault's own ledger printer.
rules: The dotted Redaction 35 cut is reserved for the lot number. Nothing else on the tile is ever set in it.
Every lot number runs at 44 px on screen and 18 pt on the printed ticket, with the grade at 9 pt.
The lot number is the first thing read: it always precedes the lot title in reading order.
Apart from the lot number, everything on the tile stays crisp. No second degraded or distressed element.
Certification digits are always set in Söhne Mono Regular, never in the Buch cut.

palette_rules.distribution: Grounds and panels are Slate Grey or Paper Neutral and nothing else. Slate Grey is the primary ground: the tile background or the stage around the slab. All type sits on Paper Neutral, as on slabvault_lot_card.pdf: the lot number, title, grade line, certification line and condition note are Vault Charcoal, and small secondary labels may be Slate Grey. Vault Charcoal also draws thin frames and keylines and is never a ground or panel. Signal Amber is the single accent: at most one hairline rule or small marker per tile, no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area, never type, a ground or a panel.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, and no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over a photograph. No drop shadow, glow or reflection is added to a slab: slabvault_house_note.txt says never add an edge, a shine or a shadow that was not there.
palette_rules.forbidden: No gold, bronze, copper, silver or other metallic effect on any type, ground, panel, rule, keyline or icon, and no bright or saturated colour there other than the single Signal Amber #C8892E accent: the house is never gilded and theatrical, never cheap and flashy. No accent colour other than Signal Amber, and no colour outside the four palette hexes (#8A9099, #1C1F24, #F2F3F4 and #C8892E) for type, grounds, panels, rules, keylines or icons.
palette_rules.photography: Photographs keep their own corrected colour: a neutral correction of the room's colour cast (warm bulb, lamp or cool bathroom light) is allowed, but the printed colours of the card or comic, the clear holder and the holder label are never recoloured toward the palette, and no palette colour is tinted into a photograph. This holds for the frame the output register binds to each tile (slabvault_consignment_2026F_01.jpg for LOT-001 through slabvault_consignment_2026F_14.jpg for LOT-014).
